models_evaluated: convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for 2D and 3D total-body photography dermoscopy

links.outcome: Dermatologist overreliance on benign CNN classification in divergent risk assessments
links.effect: Only 1.5% (n = 3/205) of dermatologists trusted a benign CNN classification over their own malignancy suspicion, despite 90.2%-96.1% reporting high trust in AI results.
links.quote: Contrarily, in divergent risk assessments, only 1.5% of dermatologists trusted a benign CNN-classification more than personal malignancy suspicion (n = 3/205).

models_evaluated: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs; specific model names not reported)

links.outcome: Patient-reported feeling of safety following AI, dermatologist, and augmented-intelligence screening
links.effect: Mean subjective safety scores were 9.5 with augmented intelligence, 7.7 with AI alone, and 9.1 with dermatologist alone; augmented intelligence exceeded AI (p < 0.0001) and dermatologist screening (p = 0.001).
links.quote: Regarding SSS, AuI induced a significantly higher feeling of safety than AI (mean-SSS (mSSS): 9.5 vs. 7.7, p < 0.0001) or dermatologist screening alone (mSSS: 9.5 vs. 9.1, p = 0.001).

links.effect: In divergent risk assessments, only 1.5% of dermatologists trusted a benign CNN classification over their own suspicion.
links.quote: Contrarily, in divergent risk assessments, only 1.5% of dermatologists trusted a benign CNN-classification more than personal malignancy suspicion (n = 3/205).

links.effect: Augmented intelligence induced a significantly higher feeling of safety than AI or dermatologist screening alone.
